about.title: About the data
about.lead: Every number in Kompas comes from open data. Here is where it comes from and what it can't tell you.
method: The city is divided into hexagons of about 0.1 km² (H3, resolution 9). For each hexagon we compute indicators such as walking minutes to the nearest stop, departures per hour, green share, noise in dB or the local price per m².
Each indicator becomes a 0–100 score compared within the same city, so a match of 80% means “fits you well in this city”.
Your emoji choices set the weights: 😐 1, 🙂 2, 😊 3, 😍 5, 🤩 8. The match is the weighted average of the criteria. Hard limits remove places instead of lowering their score.

Neighbourhood types come from clustering both cities together; a small neural network then assigns each place a type with a probability. Twin neighbourhoods are the most similar places in the other city, using only measurements that are comparable across both (walking minutes, departures and counts nearby, green share; not noise, air quality or prices, which differ in how each country measures them).
about.safety: Safety is shown only per district, based on incidents registered by the police per 1,000 residents. Registered incidents are not the same as how safe a place feels. Busy centres with many visitors register more incidents.
limits: Kraków has no official rent data and Prague no official sale-price data. Kraków prices are sale transactions (RCN); Prague prices are rents (Ministry of Finance rent map).
Where data is missing we use the city median and mark the value as estimated.
Travel times are modelled for a weekday morning, not live traffic.
Prague crime data is licensed for non-commercial use only.
